findings.title: Caller-first cancellation can be relabeled TIMEOUT by a later deadline
findings.mechanism: A caller aborts the controller first; an unsettled/non-cooperative body continues waiting. The deadline sets timedOut=true even though abort() cannot replace the first signal reason. The eventual catch selects TIMEOUT over ABORT.
findings.limit: No native-fetch exploit or new failing test execution is claimed by this historical evidence review.

findings.title: Abort propagation and stale-payload rejection do not prove prompt settlement of a non-cooperative body
findings.mechanism: The non-cooperative test explicitly resolves the body after abort. An indefinitely pending body can leave the await/finally pending. Cooperative browser body cancellation remains to be checked with delayed native JSON/blob bodies.
requiredTests: Native browser abort after headers before body completion, bounded rejection without manually completing the body
Success and error cleanup assertions for listener and timeout

findings.title: Shared CSRF bootstrap precedes request cancellation/deadline ownership
findings.mechanism: loadCsrfToken is awaited before request controller/catch/timer. Bootstrap fetch/text failures can escape the typed transport wrapper. A cancelled waiter must not cancel shared bootstrap needed by another caller.
requiredTests: Caller-local cancellation while shared CSRF promise is pending; other waiter survives
Explicit bootstrap/request deadline contract and typed failure surface

findings.title: SSE has a separate raw exception and reader lifecycle
findings.mechanism: streamRequest is unchanged by the body fix. It does not use the same HttpTransportError classification and finally does not explicitly cancel/release its reader on callback failure.
requiredTests: Native stream abort/deadline after open and no late frame delivery

findings.title: Generic transport message retains native cause; abort is not server effect cancellation
findings.mechanism: HttpTransportError keeps cause. The reviewed code rejects client payload delivery after observed abort; it does not undo a mutation, cancel a server effect, or certify telemetry redaction.
